title: ReConICS flow (one entry of the document-level flows array)
description: One directed client-to-server conversation per (client, server, protocol, server port). Only client, server and protocol are required; every other key is optional and absent when unknown. Unknown keys are ignored. See docs/data-contract.md, section Flows.

protocol.description: modbus, dnp3, enip, s7comm, snmp, ..., or unknown when nothing identifies the traffic

port.description: server port with transport, for example 502/tcp

object.description: A name Zeek logs: DNP3 object or control block type, Modbus diagnostics sub-function, S7 SZL list or block, CIP class and attribute

unit.description: Modbus unit id behind a gateway

statuses.description: How the calls ended, label to count: ok, exception: <name>, unanswered, iin: <flag>, status: <name>

portHint.description: Only on protocol unknown: the protocol the server port usually carries. Port-inferred, not dissected.

source.description: Engines that saw the conversation, joined by +: zeek, native, tshark (a conversation only tshark saw, from the optional Wireshark fallback)

portHintSource.description: Present only when portHint came from a data file instead of the built-in table: nmap-services (Nmap's port list, read from an Nmap install)

communityIds.description: Community ID v1 of the first connections Zeek saw on this conversation (policy/protocols/conn/community-id-logging). Suricata writes the same ID, so a person can pivot between the tools.

classifiedBy.description: What other open-source tools called a conversation that is still protocol unknown after Zeek, the native decoders and the port hints. A label with a confidence, never a decoded protocol: the flow's protocol stays unknown.

protocol.description: The tool's own name for it: an nDPI protocol such as TLS.Google, or the last Wireshark dissector (mapped to the PortHints names where one exists)

basis.description: dpi: nDPI deep-packet inspection; dissector: Wireshark's dissector chain (frame.protocols)

alerts.description: Suricata rule matches and protocol anomalies on this conversation, most severe first. Evidence that something looked wrong; not a decoded protocol and not proof of compromise.

severity.description: Suricata severity; 1 is the most severe
